items.stem: Write the electron dot structure of methane (CH₄) and ethane (C₂H₆).
items.answer: Methane, CH₄ : the carbon atom shares its four valence electrons with four hydrogen atoms, so carbon is surrounded by four shared electron pairs (H : C : H with one pair above and one below the carbon) and every hydrogen has two electrons. Ethane, C₂H₆ : the two carbon atoms share one electron pair with each other (C : C) and each carbon shares the remaining three electrons with three hydrogen atoms, so each carbon is again surrounded by four shared pairs.

items.stem: What is a homologous series of carbon compounds? Give an example and list its three characteristics.
items.answer: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds having similar structures and similar chemical properties in which the successive compounds differ by a —CH₂ group. Example : the alkane series CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀ … Characteristics : (i) successive members differ by one —CH₂ unit, i.e. by a mass of 14 u; (ii) all members contain the same functional group and can be represented by one general formula, so they show similar chemical properties; (iii) physical properties such as melting point, boiling point and density change gradually with increasing molecular mass.

items.stem: Why does carbon exhibit tetra covalency?
items.answer: Carbon has four valence electrons, so its valency is four. Carbon cannot lose four electrons to form a C⁴⁺ ion because that requires a very large amount of energy, which cannot be supplied to the atom; nor can it gain four electrons to form a C⁴⁻ ion, because a nucleus of only 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons. This is why carbon can only complete its octet by sharing its four valence electrons, i.e. it exhibits tetra covalency.

items.stem: An aldehyde as well as a ketone can be represented by the same molecular formula, say C₃H₆O. Write their structures and name them. State the relation between the two in the language of science.
items.answer:
Aldehyde : CH₃—CH₂—CHO, i.e. H—C(H)(H)—C(H)(H)—CHO, named propanal.
Ketone : CH₃—CO—CH₃, i.e. H₃C—C(=O)—CH₃, named propanone.
Relation : the two compounds have the same molecular formula C₃H₆O but different structures, so they are isomers (they show functional-group isomerism).

items.stem: Explain, with the help of the tetravalency of carbon, the bond formation in the CH₄ molecule.
items.answer: The CH₄ molecule is formed by the sharing of one electron of the carbon atom with one electron of each hydrogen atom. Each H atom acquires stability by having two electrons in its outermost shell through the sharing of one electron each from the H atom and the C atom. Due to the formation of 4 C—H bonds there are 8 electrons in the outermost shell of carbon and the molecule becomes stable.

items.stem: An organic compound has been obtained by reacting an unsaturated hydrocarbon with water in the presence of phosphoric acid. The compound was found to burn with a blue flame. Its mixture with water has a freezing point much below 0 °C. Identify the compound. Write the equation of the reaction by which it was formed and the reaction of its combustion.

items.stem: How can the non-biodegradable nature of detergents be reduced?
items.answer: Chemists have been able to synthesise detergents with minimum branching, i.e. with linear hydrocarbon chains, which micro-organisms can decompose. Making the chains linear makes the detergents biodegradable and so reduces their non-biodegradable nature.

items.stem: Why are soaps not suitable for washing clothes in hard water?
items.answer: Hard water contains Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ ions which react with soap to form an insoluble scum. So the soap is not able to form lather and goes waste.

items.stem: Describe the process of making soap in the laboratory.
items.answer: Take about 50 mL of cotton seed oil in a 400 mL beaker. Add to it 100 mL of 20% solution of sodium hydroxide. Heat it for about 45 minutes with constant stirring. The mixture becomes thick and the oil and water layers merge into each other. Then add about 20 g of common salt and stir the mixture. A pale yellow solid floats on the surface. It is separated and cooled. It forms a cake, which is soap.

items.stem: Explain the term alkynes with an example.
items.answer: A compound having the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (n = 2, 3, 4 …) is called an alkyne. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a carbon–carbon triple bond. The first member of the series, ethyne, has a triple bond between its two carbon atoms : H—C≡C—H.

items.stem: Give reasons for the following : Carbon only forms covalent compounds.
items.answer: Carbon can neither lose four electrons, as too much energy is required, nor gain four electrons, as its nucleus of 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons. Therefore it can only share electrons, and this is why carbon forms covalent compounds only.

items.stem: Why are alkanes called paraffins?
items.answer: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. There is no double or triple bond between any two carbon atoms, and every valency of carbon is satisfied by a single covalent bond. So they are chemically less reactive (paraffin means 'little affinity'), and this is why alkanes are called paraffins.

items.stem: (a) What is saponification? (b) Write the differences between soaps and detergents under the following heads : (i) Chemical composition, (ii) Action with hard water.
items.answer:
(a) In the saponification reaction an ester reacts with an alkali to form the salt of an acid and an alcohol :
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH (ester → salt of an acid + ethyl alcohol)
(b) (i) Chemical composition : soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids, while detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids. (ii) Action with hard water : soaps form an insoluble substance called scum with hard water, while detergents are effective in hard water because they do not form an insoluble precipitate.

items.stem: What are isomers? Draw the structures of two isomers of butane (C₄H₁₀).
items.answer:
Isomers are organic compounds having the same molecular formula but a different structural arrangement of atoms in their molecules. The two isomers of butane are :
(i) n-butane, CH₃—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃ (a straight chain of four carbons)
(ii) iso-butane (2-methylpropane), CH₃—CH(CH₃)—CH₃ (a three-carbon chain with a —CH₃ branch on the middle carbon).

items.stem: (a) Soaps cannot be used with hard water. Why? (b) Give the chemical composition of detergents. (c) Give one advantage of detergents over soaps.
items.answer: (a) Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts which react with soap and form scum (an insoluble substance). (b) Detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids. (c) Detergents do not form an insoluble precipitate with calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, so they remain effective in hard water.

items.stem: What are the advantages of synthetic detergent over soap? [Or : For cleansing action, when is a detergent preferred to a soap?]

items.stem: Explain the formation of scum when hard water is treated with soap.
items.answer: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions. These ions combine with soap molecules to form a curdy white precipitate of the calcium and magnesium salts of the soap, which is called scum.

items.stem: (a) Give a chemical test to distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons. (b) Name the products formed when ethanol burns in air. (c) Why is the reaction between methane and chlorine considered a substitution reaction?

(c) CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl. In the presence of sunlight, chlorine replaces the hydrogen atoms of methane one by one, so it is called a substitution reaction.

CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] —acetobacter→ CH₃COOH + H₂O

items.stem: How is ethanoic acid prepared commercially?
items.answer:
Ethanoic acid is prepared commercially by the reaction between methanol and carbon monoxide in the presence of iodine–rhodium as catalysts :
CH₃OH + CO —I₂–Rh→ CH₃COOH
items.ocr: Reaction arrow printed as a stray '+' after the \xrightarrow artefact; restored.

items.stem: What happens when ethanoic acid reacts with (a) sodium carbonate, (b) sodium hydroxide?
items.answer:
(a) With sodium carbonate it forms sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide :
2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + CO₂ + H₂O
(b) With sodium hydroxide it forms sodium ethanoate and water :
CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O
items.ocr: The first equation lost its arrow in print ('2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ 2CH₃COONa + CO₂'); the arrow has been restored.

items.stem: Write the electronic dot structures of (a) F₂ (b) NH₃ (c) CCl₄
items.answer:
(a) F₂ : each fluorine atom has seven valence electrons; the two atoms share one electron pair (F : F), so each fluorine has a complete octet with three lone pairs.
(b) NH₃ : nitrogen has five valence electrons; it shares three of them with three hydrogen atoms to give three N—H shared pairs and one lone pair on nitrogen.
(c) CCl₄ : carbon shares each of its four valence electrons with one chlorine atom, giving four C—Cl shared pairs; each chlorine also carries three lone pairs.
items.ocr: The printed solution is a figure on page 26 that belongs to the worked answer, so no image has been attached; the structures have been described in words.

items.stem: Mention the position of carbon on the basis of its electronic configuration and comment on the nature of the compounds formed by carbon.
items.answer: Carbon has atomic number 6, so its configuration is C(6) = 1s², 2s²2p². As it has four valence electrons, it is an element of group 14 and period 2. It can form only covalent compounds, because gaining or losing 4 electrons is impossible for it on the basis of the energy change during bond formation. So carbon always forms covalent compounds by sharing its valence electrons.

items.stem: Write the names of the following compounds : (a) CH₃—CH₂—C≡CH (b) CH₃CH₂OH (c) CH₃COCH₃
items.answer: (a) But-1-yne (butyne), (b) Ethanol, (c) Propanone.
items.ocr: Part (a) printed as 'CH CH2 - C / CH' with subscripts and the triple bond lost; restored as CH₃—CH₂—C≡CH, which matches the printed answer 'Butyne'.

items.stem: What are soaps chemically? How do they differ from synthetic detergents?
items.answer: Chemically, soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a fatty acid (a long-chain carboxylic acid). Detergents are the ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids.

items.stem: Give reasons for the following : Unsaturated hydrocarbons show addition reactions but saturated hydrocarbons do not.
items.answer: Unsaturated hydrocarbons have either double or triple bonds, one or two components of which break easily and are weak enough to form single covalent bonds with the added molecule. In comparison, saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds, which are strong. This is why unsaturated hydrocarbons show addition reactions but saturated hydrocarbons do not.

items.stem: How is it that we can use detergents for washing clothes even when the water is hard, but not soaps? What change has been made in the composition of detergents to make them biodegradable?
items.answer: Detergents are sodium salts of sulphonic acids. They can be used for washing clothes even when the water is hard, because their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble in water. Soaps are sodium salts of fatty acids; they react with Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ ions to form salts which are insoluble in water and form scum. To make detergents biodegradable their hydrocarbon chains are made linear (unbranched), so micro-organisms can decompose them.
items.ocr: The printed solution answered only the first half; the biodegradability half has been completed from the book's own explanation given for question 133/194.

items.stem: Draw the electron dot structures of : (a) C₂H₂ (b) C₂H₅OH
items.answer:
(a) C₂H₂ (ethyne) : the two carbon atoms share three electron pairs with each other (a triple bond) and each carbon shares one more pair with a hydrogen atom, H : C ⋮⋮ C : H.
(b) C₂H₅OH (ethanol) : the first carbon shares pairs with three hydrogen atoms and with the second carbon; the second carbon shares pairs with two hydrogen atoms and with the oxygen of the —O—H group, and the oxygen carries two lone pairs.

items.stem: Write the chemical equations for the two steps involved in preparing ethanol by the fermentation of molasses.
items.answer:
Fermentation is the slow decomposition of organic matter into simpler substances in the presence of enzymes. In this process the sugar of molasses is first converted into glucose and fructose in the presence of the enzyme invertase :
C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O —invertase→ C₆H₁₂O₆ + C₆H₁₂O₆
Glucose and fructose are then both converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide in the presence of another enzyme, zymase :
C₆H₁₂O₆ —zymase→ 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂
items.ocr: The word 'dioxide' came through as the artefact 'dioxion' in the array; corrected.

items.stem: An organic compound A is a constituent of an antifreeze. This compound on heating with oxygen forms another compound B which has the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. Identify the compounds A and B. Write the chemical equation of the reaction that takes place to form the compound B.
items.answer:
A is ethanol, which is used as an antifreeze. On oxidation it gives ethanoic acid, which has the molecular formula C₂H₄O₂, so B is ethanoic acid. The reaction is :
C₂H₅OH + 2[O] → CH₃COOH + H₂O
items.ocr: The printed equation lost the ethanol formula to the artefact 'C₂ (Ethanol)'; restored as C₂H₅OH. The formula of B printed as 'C H O₂'; restored as C₂H₄O₂.

items.stem: An organic compound A of molecular formula CH₂O₂ turns blue litmus red and gives brisk effervescence with Na₂CO₃. Identify A and give the chemical reaction.
items.answer:
Since compound A turns blue litmus red it is an acid. The possible acid with the formula CH₂O₂ is methanoic acid (formic acid), HCOOH. It gives brisk effervescence on reaction with Na₂CO₃ due to the evolution of carbon dioxide :
2HCOOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2HCOONa + CO₂ + H₂O

items.stem: What happens when an ester is treated with an alkali solution?
items.answer: When an ester is treated with an alkali solution such as sodium hydroxide, the ester breaks down to form the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid and the parent alcohol, for example CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH. This reaction is called the hydrolysis (saponification) of an ester.

items.stem: Write two tests to demonstrate that acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is acidic in nature.
items.answer:
(a) Acetic acid turns blue litmus red. (b) Acetic acid reacts with metals (Na, Mg, Al) to form metal ethanoates and hydrogen :
2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂

items.stem: Detergents have many advantages over soaps but are still quite harmful. Explain.
items.answer: A synthetic detergent is a better cleansing agent than soap because it works even in hard water and has a strong cleansing action. There is one major disadvantage: many synthetic detergents are non-biodegradable, so their use causes pollution of water bodies.

items.stem: What happens when an aqueous solution of potassium permanganate in NaOH solution is added to warm ethanol?
items.answer: When an aqueous solution of potassium permanganate in NaOH solution is added to warm ethanol, the purple colour of the permanganate is decolourised, because the permanganate is used up in oxidising the ethanol to ethanoic acid. When all the alcohol has been consumed the reaction stops and the purple colour persists.

items.stem: What is the disadvantage of synthetic detergent over soap?
items.answer: The disadvantage of synthetic detergent over soap is that some synthetic detergents are non-biodegradable. Hence the micro-organisms present in water bodies cannot decompose them, and this results in water pollution in rivers, lakes, etc.

items.stem: In washing powders certain chemicals are added to impart the undermentioned properties. Name the chemical used for each property : (a) keeps the dirt suspended in water, (b) removes dirt particles, (c) keeps the washing powder dry, (d) imparts whiteness.
items.answer: (a) Carboxy methyl cellulose is added to keep the dirt suspended in water. (b) Sodium carbonate is added to remove the dirt particles. (c) Sodium sulphate and sodium silicate are added to keep the washing powder dry. (d) Sodium perborate is added to impart whiteness.

items.stem: Write the name and structural formula of the simplest organic acid.
items.answer: The structural formula of the simplest organic acid is H—C(=O)—OH, i.e. HCOOH. Its common name is formic acid and its IUPAC name is methanoic acid.
items.ocr: Structural formula printed as the artefact 'z H - C - OH' with the carbonyl oxygen lost; restored as H—C(=O)—OH (HCOOH).

items.stem: An organic compound P is a constituent of wine. P on reacting with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ forms another compound Q. When a piece of sodium is added to Q, a gas R evolves which burns with a pop sound. Identify P, Q and R and write the chemical equations of the reactions involved.
items.answer:
P is ethanol, Q is ethanoic acid and R is hydrogen.
CH₃CH₂OH —acidified K₂Cr₂O₇→ CH₃COOH
2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂

items.stem: What will you observe on adding a 5% alkaline potassium permanganate solution drop by drop to some warm ethanol taken in a test tube? Write the name of the compound formed during the above chemical reaction.
items.answer: On adding KMnO₄, the pink (purple) colour of the KMnO₄ disappears initially, because it oxidises the ethanol to ethanoic acid. The name of the substance formed is ethanoic acid.

items.stem: What happens when ethanol is treated with chromic anhydride (CrO₃)? [Or : Give any one chemical equation for the oxidation of ethanol. Or : Name the product obtained when ethanol is oxidised by chromic anhydride.]
items.answer:
When ethanol is treated with chromic anhydride it is oxidised to ethanal :
CH₃CH₂OH —CrO₃ in CH₃COOH→ CH₃CHO

items.stem: Write three uses of acetic acid.
items.answer: (a) It is used in making synthetic vinegar. (b) It is used as a reagent in the chemical industry. (c) It is used for making white lead, 2PbCO₃·Pb(OH)₂.

items.stem: What happens when sodium acetate (sodium ethanoate) is heated with soda lime? What is this reaction called? Why is it called so? [Or : Name the main product formed when sodium ethanoate is heated with soda lime.]
items.answer:
(a) Methane is produced on heating sodium acetate (sodium ethanoate) with soda lime :
CH₃COONa + NaOH (CaO) —Δ→ CH₄ + Na₂CO₃
(b) This reaction is called decarboxylation, because in it a molecule of CO₂ is removed from a molecule of the acid (from its sodium salt).

items.stem: Write a test to show the presence of alcohol in an organic liquid. [Or : Give a chemical test to show/detect the presence of ethanol.]
items.answer:
Add a small piece of sodium metal to the organic liquid to be tested. If effervescence of hydrogen gas is produced, it indicates the presence of an alcohol :
2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂
The presence of hydrogen can be confirmed by bringing a burning splinter near the mouth of the test tube; it will burn with a pop sound.

items.stem: Give a chemical test to show a saponification reaction.
items.answer: Take 2 mL of ethyl ethanoate and add 4 mL of sodium hydroxide solution in a boiling tube. Two distinct layers are formed, as the two liquids are immiscible with one another. Heat the mixture in a water bath at about 330 K for 20 minutes. The ester layer, which is immiscible in water, decreases. The two immiscible layers become miscible because saponification of the ester forms sodium ethanoate and ethanol, both of which are soluble in water.

items.stem: Explain why synthetic detergents made with linear hydrocarbons are environmentally more acceptable. [Or : Explain, giving a reason, why detergents made up of molecules in which branching is minimum are preferred these days.]
items.answer: Synthetic detergents made with linear hydrocarbons are easily degraded by the micro-organisms present in water bodies like lakes, rivers, etc. This prevents water pollution, and hence they are more acceptable environmentally.
